Answers.content:
Jean needs makeup services for 6 hours each day, 4 times a week. The movie takes 5 weeks to finish.

To find the total number of days Jean needs the makeup services:
1. Calculate the number of days per week: \(4 \text{ days/week} \times 5 \text{ weeks} = 20 \text{ days}\).

This means Jean needs the makeup services for a total of 20 days.

To calculate the weekly cost, we first find the daily cost:
- Daily cost = \(6 \text{ hours/day} \times \$250/\text{hour} = \$1500\).
- Weekly cost (4 days) = \(4 \times \$1500 = \$6000\).

The total number of days Jean needs the makeup services is 20, and this affects the weekly cost calculation by determining how many times the daily cost is multiplied to get the weekly cost.

The hourly rate of the makeup artist is $250. This rate significantly affects the daily cost calculation because it determines how much Jean needs to pay for each day's makeup services.

To calculate the daily cost:
\[ \text{Daily Cost} = \text{Hourly Rate} \times \text{Number of Hours per Day} \]
\[ \text{Daily Cost} = \$250 \times 6 \]
\[ \text{Daily Cost} = \$1500 \]

This daily cost is then used in subsequent calculations to determine the weekly and total costs, as well as applying any discounts.

The discount amount applied to the total cost is 10% of the calculated total cost. This means that after calculating the total cost for the entire movie production period, Jean would receive a 10% reduction on this amount due to the significant work done.

To determine the final payment, you first calculate the daily cost by multiplying the hourly rate ($250) by the number of hours required each day (6 hours). Then, multiply the daily cost by the number of days per week (4 days) and then by the total weeks of the movie production period (5 weeks) to get the total cost. Finally, apply the 10% discount to this total cost to find out how much Jean paid.
